requirements.note: Inset-grouped list newest first, one section per day headed 'Oct 25, 2026 · $222.02'; moving an expense to another date regroups it and updates both day totals.
'This Month' card at the top of History shows $5,269.70 · October 2026 · 86 expenses and updates on add/delete.

Sheet with amount (decimal pad + Done accessory), merchant, category pull-down menu of the 7 data categories, compact date picker defaulting to today, optional note. Save disabled for empty or -5; new row appears under today.
Tapping a row opens an Edit Expense sheet; merchant/date edits save and regroup. Swipe left shows a system Delete action that removes the row and updates totals.
Categories tab lists this month's 7 categories largest first with '29% of total · 16 expenses' and amount; tapping one pushes its this-month transactions grouped by day.
All amounts formatted $1,544.59; add, edit and delete all survive relaunch.

bugs: Cancel on a filled-in New Expense sheet discards silently, with no confirmation.
The 'Enter an amount greater than zero.' footer shows on a blank form before the user has typed anything, and the form jumps when it goes away.
tells: Category rows on the Categories screen push a detail view but have no disclosure chevron.
Merchant field has only a placeholder, no label, while Amount has a label, so the first section is inconsistent.
Nothing marks a category besides its name: no colour or icon anywhere, so the Categories screen has no visual share indicator (percentage text only).
Day-section headers scroll away instead of staying pinned (plain inset-grouped style; acceptable, but a long date-grouped history usually keeps the day visible).
A.scroll: Smooth and native: slow drags track the finger, flings decelerate naturally, the large title collapses and pull-past-top rubber-bands with no blank or popping rows. Scroll position and an open swipe action survive switching tabs.

requirements.note: Newest first, grouped by day with 'Sunday, Oct 25' on the left and the day total right-aligned; date edits regroup correctly and an added expense lands under 'Today'.
'THIS MONTH / October 2026 / $5,269.70 / 86 expenses this month' card with a stacked per-category colour bar, updating on add/edit/delete.

Large amount field (decimal pad + Done), merchant, category pushed picker with icons and checkmark (7 categories), date defaulting to today, optional note. Saving empty shows inline red errors on amount and merchant; -5 is rejected.
Rows (with chevrons) open an Edit sheet that also has a Delete expense button; edits regroup. Swipe left shows a system Delete action that removes the row and updates the day total.
Categories tab lists categories largest first with amount, 29.3% share, expense count and a progress bar; tapping one pushes its transactions with a This month / All time segmented control.
Currency formatted throughout; add, edit and delete all survive relaunch.

tells: Warm off-white/peach custom palette and an orange-red brand tint replace system grouped backgrounds. It is tasteful, but it reads as designed rather than stock.
The monthly total uses a condensed heavy display font that is not SF, and it barely grows at the largest text size.
Category picker rows expose no accessibility labels (unlabelled cells), so VoiceOver would not read them properly.
Category detail rows repeat the category name ('Health') under every merchant.
Notes are not shown in the list rows, so a note is only visible after opening the edit sheet.
Day-section headers scroll away rather than pinning.
B.scroll: Smooth and native, with natural fling deceleration and rubber-banding. Pulling down at the top reveals a system search field the way Mail does; no blank rows or jumps were seen.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and persist correctly, and both scroll and adapt to dark mode and the largest text size well. B adds the details a careful iOS app has: a discard-changes confirmation, inline validation messages, category icons and share bars, chevrons on rows you can tap, a This month/All time filter and search. A is plainer and closer to stock, but it discards edits silently and shows its validation message too early. B's custom warm palette costs it a little platform fidelity, but it is the app I would rather ship.
